bib.title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents

question: How well can LLM-based agents complete realistic, long-horizon web tasks in a reproducible, self-hosted environment with functional-correctness evaluation?
hypothesis: Limited LLM performance stems from a lack of capabilities such as active exploration and failure recovery.
contributions: WebArena: a standalone, self-hostable environment of four functional websites (e-commerce, forum, GitLab, CMS) plus map, calculator, scratchpad, Wikipedia and manuals
A benchmark of 812 long-horizon tasks with programmatic functional-correctness validators
Baseline LLM agents (GPT-4, GPT-3.5, text-bison-001) with and without CoT, and error analysis

method.summary: Docker-hosted websites built from open-source software with sampled real-world data; 812 natural-language intents (241 templates) scored by answer matching or programmatic state checks. Baselines are few-shot (2 examples) LLM agents that read an accessibility tree and emit one action at a time, with or without CoT, and with or without an unachievable-task hint.
method.task: web navigation / agent task completion from high-level natural-language intents

datasets.name: WebArena benchmark
datasets.source: authors' annotation; reference answers by authors and one external annotator, each annotated twice, third annotator on disagreement

datasets.name: WebArena websites
datasets.size: E-commerce ~90k products, 300+ categories; Reddit 95 subreddits, 127390 posts, 661781 users; GitLab 300 repos, 1000+ accounts; map confined to northeast US; Wikipedia (Kiwix) cutoff May 2023
datasets.source: Magento, Postmill, GitLab, OpenStreetMap, Kiwix; data sampled from real counterparts and the Webshop dump
datasets.preprocessing: Docker images reset to deterministic initial state

inference.temperature: 1.0 (0.0 for the GPT-3.5 replication in Table 5)
inference.samples: inferred: one run per task and configuration; no seeds or repeats reported
inference.prompting: System message with environment, actions and rules, plus 2 in-context examples; direct agent emits action only, CoT agent reasons ('Let's think step-by-step') then emits action after 'In summary, the next action I will perform is'; observation is accessibility tree with element IDs, URL, open tabs, previous action; UA hint = 'If you believe the task is impossible to complete, provide the answer as "N/A" in the bracket.'

parameters.early_stop: same action repeated more than 3 times on the same observation, or 3 consecutive invalid actions
parameters.text_bison_retries: up to 10 retries until a valid action

metrics.name: SR (end-to-end task success rate)
metrics.definition: fraction of 812 tasks with reward 1; info-seeking via exact_match, must_include or fuzzy_match (gpt-4-0613); other tasks via programmatic state checks (locator plus keyword match)

metrics.name: SR_UA
metrics.definition: success rate on unachievable tasks (agent must answer N/A)

eval.protocol: Single run at temperature 1.0; fuzzy_match checked by hand on 40 examples (39 agree); no confidence intervals or repeated seeds.

prompts.text: Help a teacher to grade the answer of a student given a question. Keep in mind that the student may use different phrasing or wording to answer the question. The goal is to evaluate whether the answer is semantically equivalent to the reference answer. question: {{intent}} reference answer: {{reference answer}} all the string 'N/A' that you see is a special sequence that means 'not achievable' student answer: {{prediction}} Conclude the judgement by correct/incorrect/partially correct.
See Fig 7 (reasoning agent), Fig 8 (CoT examples), Fig 9 (direct agent), Fig 10 (direct examples) in the appendix; not copied in full.

results.claim: Best GPT-4 agent (CoT, no UA hint) reaches 14.41% end-to-end success versus 78.24% for humans.
results.setup: WebArena, 812 tasks, accessibility-tree observation, 2-shot prompt, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.9, max 30 state transitions, single run; GPT-4-0613, CoT, UA hint removed
results.quote: our best GPT-4-based agent only achieves an end-to-end task success rate of 14.41%, significantly lower than the human performance of 78.24%

results.claim: GPT-4 with CoT and the unachievable (UA) hint scores 11.70%.
results.setup: WebArena, 812 tasks, accessibility-tree observation, 2-shot prompt, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.9, max 30 state transitions, single run; GPT-4, CoT, UA hint
results.quote: GPT-4 (OpenAI, 2023) with CoT prompting achieves a modest end-to-end task success rate of 11.70%

results.claim: Human success rate on a sample of one task from each of 170 templates is 78.24%, lower on information-seeking tasks (74.68%) than others (81.32%).
results.setup: 5 CS graduate students, one task from each of 170 templates, avg time 110s
results.quote: the human annotators complete 78.24% of the tasks, with lower performance on information-seeking tasks
results.table: Table 2 / inline table, Success Rate_all 78.24%; info 74.68%; others 81.32%

results.claim: About 50% of human failures are misinterpreting the intent, incomplete answers or incomplete executions; the rest are off-target executions.
results.quote: we found that 50% of the failures are due to misinterpreting the intent

results.claim: CoT reasoning improves GPT-3.5 by 2.34 points (6.41 to 8.75) with UA hint.
results.setup: WebArena, 812 tasks, accessibility-tree observation, 2-shot prompt, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.9, max 30 state transitions, single run; GPT-3.5-turbo-16k-0613, UA hint on
results.quote: The explicit reasoning procedure is somewhat helpful, it brings 2.34% improvement over the version without it.

results.claim: GPT-3.5 with CoT and UA hint scores 8.75%.
results.setup: WebArena, 812 tasks, accessibility-tree observation, 2-shot prompt, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.9, max 30 state transitions, single run; GPT-3.5, CoT, UA hint
results.quote: GPT-3.5 (OpenAI, 2022) with CoT prompting is only able to successfully perform 8.75% of the tasks.

results.claim: text-bison-001 with CoT and UA hint scores 5.05%, below GPT-3.5.
results.setup: WebArena, 812 tasks, accessibility-tree observation, 2-shot prompt, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.9, max 30 state transitions, single run; text-bison-001, CoT, UA hint; up to ten retries for a valid action
results.quote: TEXT-BISON-001 (Anil et al., 2023) underperforms GPT-3.5, with a success rate of 5.05%

results.claim: The UA hint makes GPT-4 wrongly declare 54.9% of feasible tasks impossible (early stopping).
results.setup: WebArena, 812 tasks, accessibility-tree observation, 2-shot prompt, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.9, max 30 state transitions, single run; GPT-4 CoT with UA hint
results.quote: GPT-4 erroneously identifies 54.9% of feasible tasks as impossible.

results.quote: GPT-4 retains the capacity to recognize 44.44% of such tasks

results.table: Table 2, row GPT-4 CoT no UA hint, column SR_AC

results.setup: WebArena, 812 tasks, accessibility-tree observation, 2-shot prompt, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.9, max 30 state transitions, single run; GPT-3.5, direct, no UA hint

results.quote: we manually checked 40 examples and found that 39 of them are identical to our human judgment

results.claim: Authors hypothesise that missing active exploration and failure recovery limit current LLMs.
results.setup: Stated explanation; not tested by an intervention
results.quote: We hypothesize that the limited performance of current LLMs stems from a lack of crucial capabilities such as active exploration and failure recovery

results.claim: GPT-4 agent latches onto the first related information (observation bias) and ignores already-entered input, repeating the same type action until the step limit.
results.setup: Qualitative examples from error analysis, GPT-4 agent; no frequencies given
results.quote: the agent disregards this detail and continuously issues the command type [2430] [DMV area] until it reaches the maximum step limit

limits: Single run per configuration at temperature 1.0 with no variance; GPT-3.5 temperature 0.0 replication given for only one configuration (6.28).
Failure explanations (no exploration, poor failure recovery, dialogue fine-tuning) are hypotheses; error analysis is qualitative with no failure-category frequencies.
Only three LLMs, text-only accessibility-tree observations, 2-shot prompting, no memory or planning-search agents; authors note such methods as future testbed.
Human baseline from 5 CS graduate students on 170 sampled tasks; authors concede domain knowledge differences.
Models dated: GPT-4-0613 era; 14.41% since superseded by later agents (not covered in this paper).
Map covers northeast US only; GPT-4-judged fuzzy_match tested on 40 manual examples.
